title: Inside ContextCast
subtitle: From structured evidence to a narrated, portable briefing.
provenance: Conceptual overview of this repository. The sequence diagram simplifies controller and browser events. No external service is contacted by the viewer.

sources.label: Repository architecture · module map
sources.excerpt: src/schema/briefing.ts validates content. scripts/build-briefing.ts bundles the player and Mermaid into one HTML file. src/player/controller.ts owns the current beat and utterance generation. src/player/speech.ts adapts browser speech. src/renderers/scenes.ts renders six layouts. The viewer never fetches briefing data or audio.

items.title: Browser narration
items.body: Speak short beats on explicit Play.

beats.speech: ContextCast separates research from presentation. The author collects evidence and writes a structured briefing, while the same player handles every generated artifact.
The compiler validates that content, bundles the viewer and diagram library, and produces one file that opens directly from disk.
Narration remains text until you press Play. The browser uses your selected voice, and the controller advances when each short utterance finishes.

visual.description: Conceptual sequence. Speech completion advances the beat; boundary events are optional and unused.
visual.definition:
sequenceDiagram
 participant V as Viewer
 participant C as Controller
 participant S as Browser speech
 V->>C: Play
 C->>V: Render current beat
 C->>S: Speak one utterance
 S-->>C: End event
 C->>V: Select next beat
 C->>S: Speak next utterance

beats.speech: The controller owns the active beat. It updates the visual and sends one utterance to the browser, rather than queueing the whole briefing.
Seeking invalidates old callbacks before cancellation. This prevents an old completion event from advancing the new chapter or starting a second narration stream.

cue.text: One controller · one active beat · generation-checked callbacks

beats.speech: The timeline estimates duration from word counts. It is useful for navigation, while the real speech completion event remains authoritative for advancement.
